overview: White offers a pawn with f3 before developing the knight on c3, so Black has extra options such as 3...Nc6, 3...f5 or 3...e5 4.dxe5 Qxd1+. After 3...exf3 4.Nxf3 White has open lines and a lead in development for a pawn. It is a trappy gambit that is rarely seen from strong players.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture on f3 with the knight, develop Bd3 and Bf4, castle and attack f7 or h7.
Use the open f-file and quick development to attack before Black consolidates.

black_ideas.idea: Decline with ...e5 to trade queens and reach a sound endgame.

typical_structures.structure: White d4 pawn with open e- and f-files; Black pawn on d5 gone, extra pawn on e-file side.

character.notes: Open attacking play for the pawn, with traps; both sides can lose fast.

gambit.notes: Black can accept and hold the pawn with accurate play.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious: Black has the simple 3...e5 and other good replies; compensation is thought insufficient.

structure.notes: Open centre and files after exf3; central pawns come off quickly.

approach.notes: Rarely chosen by strong players; played for surprise and traps.

level.notes: Traps and theory to know; a dubious line is not for a first repertoire.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...e5
sublines_that_differ.how: Queenless endgame with White's king displaced; no real attack.

character.reason: Open attack against a pawn up, with traps.

gambit.reason: White gives a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Compensation is considered inadequate against good defence.

structure.reason: Open lines and files straight away.

level.reason: Dubious, so never beginner; traps and sidelines to memorise.

plans.reason: Pawn for time and an attack on the king.
